summary: No NGPC page readable (outdoornebraska.gov and the atlas viewer both refuse plain HTTP), so nothing confirmed. Camping is informal pull-off/parking-area camping along the WMA's gravel road beside I-80: ownership wma is the right class (not agency-designated sites). Sand rule passes on imagery (gravel lot and road). Pin is the gravel lot at the west tip of a ~15-acre sandpit lake off the I-80 Minden interchange.
flags: INCLUSION (wildlife-agency rule): what every source I could read describes is pull-off camping - 'pull-offs along a gravel road' (The Dyrt), a gravel lot off I-80 - with no numbered or agency-designated sites. Under the rule that is a parking-lot/pull-off allowance, which is exactly what the `wma` class is for, and the entry is already `wma`; no change proposed. NGPC's own current wording on camping at Bassway Strip could not be read (outdoornebraska.gov Cloudflare block; the 2025-26 Public Access Atlas is a JavaScript viewer), so the 3-night limit rests on camper sites and on the atlas rule NGPC prints for neighbouring Platte WMAs ('Camping limited to three consecutive nights in a six-day consecutive period'). A human with a browser could check the atlas row.

SAND RULE passes on imagery: the access is a graded gravel road and a gravel turnaround lot off the I-80 ramp; no open beach or sand flat is used for parking. The Platte's sandbars lie ~250 m south behind woods.

WATERFRONT not waterfront kept, lead: the stored pin is the gravel lot at the west tip of a sandpit lake (~520 x 120 m, roughly 15 acres, over the pond line), 20-40 m from the water with a thin fringe of trees; the gravel road continues east along the lake's north shore behind a treeline. With no designated sites I can't tie any camping spot to the shore, so the value stays down. I-80 is ~150 m north.
